problem:
Which of the following augmented matrices are **not** in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 4 & 9 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -1 & 6 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Augmented Matrices in Row Echelon Form
examples.problem:
Which of the following augmented matrices are in row echelon form?
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071571/assets/34184a95be2b3ae6865fde109ace7e8b4397f4b01982928be73cff4199792d61.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Remember that an augmented matrix is in row echelon form if its coefficient matrix satisfies the following conditions:

- All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

- Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The first matrix is not in row echelon form since $a_{32} \neq 0$ (condition II is violated).
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071571/assets/b9f56d3f0414f4b56b50e59c2c02d9072f1fb74ce09d801a1ab62abac61ad737.png)

- The second matrix is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071571/assets/8562a693df46625ee0dc2bcdecc664dfc50a99889fdb855ae2e06dc1db02a3d4.png)

- The third matrix is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071571/assets/d263bfe2386309c55f1d63d97d15eaa682e9b0748a9bee6d3378d0b9035927ba.png)

- The fourth matrix is not in row echelon form since, for example, the leading entry $a_{22}$ lies to the left of the leading entry $a_{13}$ (condition II is violated).
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071571/assets/6ccb00b5e1387cd15847c50d66b26ee903d95428bcff2bfc933b675f9b590717.png)

feedback.problem:
Which of the following matrices are **not** in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that a matrix is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

- All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.
- Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is not in row echelon form since the second row contains only zeros and it is not at the bottom of the matrix (condition I is violated).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is not in row echelon form since the leading entry ${c}_{32}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated). 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $B$ and $C$ are **not** in row echelon form.
